issues.description: The solution (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm) pushes an extraneous immediate value before the format string: lines 14-16 show `push 123` followed by `push hello` and `call printf`. The template (template_repository/helloWorld.asm) pushes only the format string (`push hello` at lines 15-16) and the problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 21-22) instructs that the format string should be passed before any arguments. The extra `push 123` in the solution introduces an unnecessary argument on the stack and therefore contradicts the template and the exercise guidance, which may confuse students about the intended use/order of arguments when calling printf.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the extraneous `push 123` from solution_repository/helloWorld.asm (line 14) so the solution matches the template and the exercise guidance (only `push hello` then `call printf`). If the intent is to demonstrate passing an argument to printf, update the problem statement to clarify stack push ordering and provide a matching example in both template and solution (or reorder pushes and add a format placeholder so the extra argument is meaningful).
